subject: Cross-region technical deep-dive: DST-safe slot proposal and fallback plan
messages:
From: Martin Lowe <martin.lowe@vertexcloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, salesops@vertexcloud.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Cross-region technical deep-dive: finding overlap across APAC/EU/US

Diego / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Our architects (Ayesha in Bangalore, Tom in Frankfurt, and myself in New York) are keen to do a 90–120 minute technical deep-dive next week to validate model routing, KV cache behavior, and secure egress patterns. We ran availability against our calendar and attached a short constraints sheet (vertex_constraints.xlsx).

High level asks:
- 90–120 minutes, prefer live run-through of a sample workload and Q&A with our infra team.
- We need a DST-safe option because our Frankfurt team has a partial-permanent flex schedule and daylight-savings transitions cause confusion when coordinating with APAC.
- Two fallback slots in case of last-minute travel.

Raw availability from our side (all local times):
- Ayesha (Bangalore): 09:00–11:30 IST or 18:00–20:00 IST (best window: 18:00 IST)
- Tom (Frankfurt, CET): 09:00–12:00 CET or 16:00–18:30 CET
- Martin (NYC, EST): 08:00–11:00 EST or 17:00–19:00 EST

We recognize there may be only small overlap. Can you propose 3 candidate windows (including at least one with short-hours overlap using an engineer rotation) and include a fallback single-region run if a full tri-region session is impossible?

Attachment: vertex_constraints.xlsx (spreadsheet with individual names and blocked times)

Cheers,
Martin Lowe
VP Solutions, VertexCloud
[m] +1 347 555 0198

---
Note: For any calendar invites please hold off until we confirm internal stakeholders.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lowe <martin.lowe@vertexcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:01:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Cross-region technical deep-dive: finding overlap across APAC/EU/US

Martin — thanks, got the constraints file. Looping in Marissa (SE lead) and Ethan (platform engineer) to propose concrete windows and DST-safe fallbacks. We can definitely run a tri-region 90-min session if we accept a partial overlap and rotate the live demo responsibilities.

Quick internal notes: please see below for the raw availability translated to UTC so we can reason about overlaps: (converted from their sheet)
- Ayesha (BOM) 09:00–11:30 IST => 03:30–06:00 UTC; 18:00–20:00 IST => 12:30–14:30 UTC
- Tom (FRA) 09:00–12:00 CET => 08:00–11:00 UTC; 16:00–18:30 CET => 15:00–17:30 UTC
- Martin (NYC) 08:00–11:00 EST => 13:00–16:00 UTC; 17:00–19:00 EST => 22:00–00:00 UTC

Initial observation: the best UTC overlap windows look to be 13:00–14:30 UTC (Martin late morning, Tom mid-afternoon, Ayesha early evening) and a narrower 12:30–14:30 UTC slot if Ayesha chooses her evening slot. We need to build two variants:
- Full tri-region 90-min (primary): target 13:00–14:30 UTC
- Two-stage fallback (secondary): 45–60 min tri-region warmup + follow-up recorded deep-dive with APAC-only hands-on run

Marissa / Ethan — can you sketch 3 candidate options (UTC) and list who will take the live demo segments (routing demo / KV cache / network egress)? Also note any constraints related to DST or local office holidays we should be mindful of.

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Martin Lowe <martin.lowe@vertexcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Cross-region technical deep-dive: finding overlap across APAC/EU/US

Diego / Ethan — I translated the constraints and ran a quick availability sweep using our timezone matrix (redwood-dawg-timezone-matrix.csv). Here are three candidate plans with explicit DST-safe notes. I left Martin on the thread so Vertex can confirm quickly.

Plan A — Primary tri-region (best effort, 90 minutes)
- UTC slot: 13:00–14:30 UTC (Tue/Wed preferred)
- Who leads: Marissa (routing & orchestration 13:00–13:30), Ethan (KV cache / perf 13:30–14:05), Diego (networking/security 14:05–14:30)
- DST notes: CET/CEST transitions are static for this date range; ensure calendar invites are sent in UTC to avoid local DST auto-conversions.
- Backup: If APAC cannot join the full 90 mins, run a 45-min tri-region intro (13:00–13:45 UTC) then schedule APAC deep follow-up at 12:30–13:30 IST next day.

Plan B — Rotating live segments (reduces inconvenience for APAC)
- UTC slot: 12:30–14:00 UTC (gives Ayesha 18:00–19:30 IST)
- Who leads: Ethan starts (12:30–13:00), Marissa 13:00–13:40, Diego 13:40–14:00
- DST notes: Use explicit timezone labels in calendar (avoid floating "local" view). Add a calendar note: "Times shown in UTC; see participant local times in event description."

Plan C — Two-stage (safer fallback)
- Stage 1 (tri-region): 13:00–13:30 UTC (overview, architecture, Q&A)
- Stage 2 (APAC deep dive): 12:30–13:30 IST next day (hands-on, runbook, network traces)
- Who leads: Stage1 Marissa; Stage2 Ethan + Ayesha (customer leads hands-on)

Attachments: I attached a small network-diagram-stub.png and the timezone CSV with explicit conversions. Also added a short checklist for invites (include UTC times, explicit local times for each attendee, and a point-person for recording and notes).

If Vertex confirms Plan A or B, I can create the calendar invite with explicit UTC and local-times in body and include the recording + Slack channel for troubleshooting. If they want C, we should confirm availability for the APAC follow-up before sending invites.

Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lowe <martin.lowe@vertexcloud.com>, Ayesha Rao <ayesha.rao@vertexcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, salesops@vertexcloud.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:30:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Cross-region technical deep-dive: DST-safe slot proposal and fallback plan

Martin / Ayesha — thanks for the fast turnaround. Marissa proposed three clear options; our preference is Plan A (13:00–14:30 UTC) or Plan B (12:30–14:00 UTC) depending on Ayesha's preference for the APAC evening slot. Please confirm which plan you prefer and which two calendar dates next week work for you. Once confirmed we will:

- Draft a calendar invite using explicit UTC and each participant's local time (no floating timezones)
- Assign live demo owners per time block and include a 10-minute buffer for handoffs
- Create a recording + Slack channel; Ethan will own the live runbook and test recording before the session

Fallbacks: if APAC cannot join live we will run Plan C (45-min tri-region intro + APAC follow-up).

Proposed dates (pick two):
- Tue 17 Nov 2026
- Wed 18 Nov 2026
- Thu 19 Nov 2026 (alternate)

Attachment: redwood-dawg-timezone-matrix.csv (UTC conversions included).

Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
